contexts.text: A fallacy of sense... that there are simple substances, which are monads and atoms. See DLW 229.
(Such) cannot but terminate the ideas of their thought in the atoms of Epicurus, or in the monads of Leibnitz, or in the subtile substances of Wolff...

Leibnitz said... that he had indeed acknowledged monads as unities: but that there were in them simpler and purer substances, by means of which the monad has been formed, from which came forth the changes of state therein... and Leibnitz therefore wondered that Wolff had maintained his monad to be created out of nothing; and, when divided, to fall into nothing...
